assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson at the LHC is a discovery in the plainest sense: it confirmed the last missing piece of the Standard Model and the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. The 2013 prize recognized the theory; the experimental observation is the natural counterpart and its importance and clarity are not in doubt.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the hard part. The discovery rests on two large collaborations and an accelerator project. A three-person configuration from the supplied names could pair the machine (Evans) with the two experiments' leadership (Gianotti for ATLAS, Virdee for CMS), but Jenni and Della Negra are equally defensible founders of ATLAS and CMS, so the choice is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: two independent experiments, large later datasets, and measured couplings consistent with the Standard Model. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue relative to the 2013 theory prize.
uncertainties: Whether a fair three-person split exists among the five credited names; I cannot independently verify individual leadership roles.
Prize rules limit laureates to three while the work is collective, which some members may see as a decisive obstacle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase established that gauge potentials and geometric phases have physical, observable consequences. The ideas are conceptually deep, widely applied (molecular physics, optics, topological matter) and clearly formulated.
assessment.attribution: Attribution to Aharonov (with Bohm, who is deceased and not credited here) and Berry is reasonably clean for two parts of one theme. Related precursors (Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam) are a known complication I recall but have not verified here.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades (electron-interference and optical/molecular geometric-phase experiments) and thoroughly stable; recognition is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The discovery combines two related but distinct results that might be judged separately.
Priority questions concerning earlier work (Ehrenberg-Siday, Pancharatnam) and the death of Bohm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision mapping of the CMB anisotropies (WMAP, Planck and ground experiments) fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent level and tested inflationary predictions of nearly scale-invariant adiabatic fluctuations. This is clear discovery-driven cosmology with enormous lasting impact; the 2006 prize covered only the COBE detection of the spectrum and first anisotropies.
assessment.attribution: WMAP leadership (Bennett as PI, Page as instrument and Spergel as theory/analysis lead) gives a coherent trio; Puget's role is as a Planck HFI leader and is a rival claim of equal standing. Collaborative nature makes any selection somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature and independently confirmed by WMAP, Planck, ACT and SPT; recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Choice between WMAP and Planck leaders is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter as a whole new platform. It is a case of prediction plus experiment with strong originality and a rapidly growing field.
assessment.attribution: A theory-plus-experiment configuration is natural: Bistritzer and MacDonald for the continuum-model prediction, Jarillo-Herrero for the experimental discovery. Other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) and Cao as lead student complicate the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many laboratories, though the superconducting mechanism and some correlated phases are still debated. Recognition is plausible but possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Whether MacDonald and Bistritzer or other theorists (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) deserve the theory credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpin proposals for redefining the second, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The invention is original and the impact on precision measurement is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori's invention of the magic-wavelength scheme is decisive; Ye's realization of the highest-performance clocks is a strong second contribution. A two-person prize looks fair, though the 2005 and 2012 prizes already touched related frequency-comb and ion-clock work.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with multiple independent laboratories achieving comparable accuracy; the redefinition of the second is still pending, so recognition could be timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier comb and trapped-ion clock prizes.
Contributions of other groups (e.g. Hollberg, Ludlow, Bloom/Ye vs. Ludlow) are not assessed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (2013) and the TXS 0506+056 and Galactic-plane associations opened neutrino astronomy and constrain cosmic-ray accelerators. It is a clear experimental discovery of a new window on the universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen (leading IceCube and the concept), Karle and Spiering have clear leadership roles, but the collaboration is large and the AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES precursors complicate credit.
assessment.maturity: Strong statistical significance and corroborating associations, though source identification is still incomplete; recognition is plausible.
uncertainties: The origin of most events remains unresolved.
Alternative candidates for leadership credit among the collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* provided direct visual evidence of black-hole shadows and tests of general relativity at strong field. The work is a striking and clearly understood achievement of very-long-baseline interferometry.
assessment.attribution: Falcke (shadow proposal), Doeleman (EHT founding director) and Moran (VLBI technique) form a plausible set, but the collaboration includes hundreds, and earlier theory (Bardeen, Luminet) and instrumentation contributors may merit consideration.
assessment.maturity: Recent and still being improved; independent images from different years agree, but the interpretation of polarization and spin is evolving, and the 2020 prize already honored black-hole physics.
uncertainties: Possibly premature relative to later confirmation.
Overlap with the 2020 black-hole prize and diffuse credit within a very large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the HgTe experimental realization, created a major branch of condensed-matter physics with lasting conceptual impact beyond the 2016 topological-phase prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele (theory) and Molenkamp (experimental confirmation) form a compact configuration; however, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and others contributed key proposals for HgTe, so the credit is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in several materials and now well established, although practical applications and some claims have been slow.
uncertainties: Strong competing claims from Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes are outside the supplied credit.
Relation to the 2016 prize may reduce urgency.
